subject: Post-call: Globex competitive bench follow-ups (latency & throughput tests)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@globex.com>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Mar 2026 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap: initial latency/throughput questions and next tests

Hi Rajesh / Maya —

Thanks again for carving out time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

What we heard from you:
- You’re running a latency-sensitive chat feature and evaluating Redwood vs your current hyperscaler (AWS Bedrock) for inference costs and p95/p99 latency.
- Primary goals: p95 under ~200ms for short assistant responses, predictable scaling to ~250 concurrent sessions, and lower per-token cost.
- You’d like empirical A/B numbers on your actual prompt set (8k token context mix) and tail latency (p99) under load.

What we (Redwood) propose next:
1) We’ll run an A/B benchmark using your 200-sample prompt set (you mentioned the QA + summary flows) against Bedrock and Redwood hosted endpoints.
2) Measure p50/p95/p99, tokens/sec, and end-to-end throughput at 1, 8, and 32 concurrent requests.
3) Share raw CSV + charts, and a short action plan with recommended config (batching, KV cache, quantization profile).

Deliverables & timing:
- Initial bench (AWS Bedrock vs Redwood hosted) and CSV by EOD Mon 3/2.
- Follow-up call Wed 3/3 to review numbers and align on a live run in your VPC (if you want private testing).

Attachments we’ll share: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-benchmarks-20260301.csv, GLBX-action-plan-20260301.docx.

Questions for you (quick):
- Can you confirm the sample prompt set location (Drive link or we can pull from the HubSpot repo)?
- Any hard constraints on p99 latency (e.g., must be <500ms)?

I’ve looped in Dylan (AE) and Rishi (SE) — Dylan will coordinate scheduling; Rishi will run the tests.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123
Redwood Inference

Hey Rajesh —

Thanks for the upload, we pulled the _8kcontext set. Quick note on test plan before Rishi runs the job: 

Planned runs (all against the same model family for parity):
- Single-request latency (cold vs warm) with 512-token response target (p50/p95/p99).
- Concurrency sweep: 1, 8, 32 concurrent workers measuring aggregate tokens/sec and per-request tail latency.
- A/B compare Redwood hosted endpoint vs Bedrock endpoint using the same model config + prompt.

Preliminary hypothesis based on our infra: Redwood should show lower tail latency and higher tokens/sec for medium-length responses because of our continuous batching and KV cache. We’ll surface both absolute numbers and percent delta.

I attached a short action plan doc (GLBX-action-plan-20260301.docx) that lays out who does what for the Wed run (VPC vs hosted).

Proposed times for Wed 3/3 live run: 10:30 PT or 14:00 PT. Which do you prefer?

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Rajesh Patel <rajesh@globex.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Mar 2026 08:43:51 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap: initial latency/throughput questions and next tests

Rajesh —

We ran the initial A/B jobs this morning against the uploaded prompt set (200 samples, mix of QA + summarization) using the following test environment:
- Redwood hosted endpoint (n1): hosted cluster (4x A100-equivalent nodes), model: open-llama-70b-quant (produces similar quality to your Bedrock baseline).
- Bedrock baseline (n2): MegaCloud/AWS Bedrock managed endpoint (A100-equivalent).

High-level results (short summary, full CSV attached as redwood-vs-hyperscaler-benchmarks-20260301.csv):
- Single-request (512-token target):
  - Redwood: p50 32ms, p95 110ms, p99 210ms, tokens/sec ~480
  - Bedrock: p50 48ms, p95 185ms, p99 420ms, tokens/sec ~320
- Concurrency (8 concurrent workers, same 512-token target):
  - Redwood aggregate tokens/sec ~380, median per-request p95 130ms, p99 260ms
  - Bedrock aggregate tokens/sec ~260, median per-request p95 240ms, p99 520ms
- Notes: Bedrock showed higher variance on tails during concurrent bursts; Redwood’s KV caching and continuous batching reduced queuing and improved tokens/sec.

Attached: redwood-vs-hyperscaler-benchmarks-20260301.csv, latency-throughput-summary-20260302.png. Charts in the PNG highlight the p95 and p99 gap and tokens/sec across concurrency.

Next technical suggestions:
- If you want sub-200ms p95 consistently, enable per-customer KV prefix caching and a small batching window (10–20ms) — tradeoff is slightly higher p50 but much better p95.
- For the Wed live run in your VPC, we’ll bring the same kernel and quantization settings and instrument with tracing so we can correlate spikes.

I’m available on Wed 3/3 at 10:30 PT for the live run — we can also do 14:00 PT if you prefer.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
